name: boredom
description: A perception that the current set of experiences is too slow or repetitive.
perceptions: What I'm experiencing now is stale.
results: looking for something different to do

guidance.description: The best way to overcome boredom may be to explore and identify why you feel bored in the first place.

variations.name: bored with inactivity
variations.description: A perception that you need more mental or physical stimulation.
results: try to find something to do

guidance.description: Waiting room boredom is real, and doesn’t appear to be improving. Cartoonists and comedians have had much to say about the long wait times in the healthcare provider’s office, and as is often the case, there is some truth behind these witticisms.

variations.name: ennui
variations.description: A general pattern of being weary and dissatisfied about everything in life.
perceptions: Everything is kinda boring and annoying.

guidance.description: Ennui is the slow tide that can pull you away from the joy in life. It is more than boredom and not quite depression. It can touch anyone, no matter how life looks on the outside. Knowing what ennui is helps you see the signs early.

commentaries.quote: Boredom can be the motherhood of creativity.

Boredom is a catalyst for change and an opportunity for reflection. Therefore, the feeling may arise during a task that isn’t challenging or is extremely repetitive. It can emerge due to a lack of self-awareness about what we find fulfilling. Personality traits also play a role—those prone to sensation seeking, extraversion, and novelty may be more likely to experience boredom.

In a 2014 study called ‘The challenges of the disengaged mind‘, participants were placed in a room alone, for up to 15 minutes, with nothing to do but think. They also had the choice to give themselves an electric shock by pushing a button placed next to them. Even though there was absolutely no pressure on the participants to shock themselves (and many of them said they’d pay money to avoid the shock beforehand), 25% of women and 67% of men still chose to push the button. Put simply – people would rather experience physical pain than be bored.
commentaries.attribution: Ali Abdaal in 'The Hidden Power of Boredom'

commentaries.quote: I've got a great ambition to die of exhaustion rather than boredom.

Instead of running away from boredom, we should invite it wholeheartedly, 'Come as you are,' we say to boredom itself. 'Teach me your lessons. Teach me about the reality of time, the shallowness of desire, and myself.'
